chordInfo.name: Half-Diminished Chords
chordInfo.subtitle: Master the bittersweet tension of half-diminished chords - the essential ii chord in minor keys and a cornerstone of jazz voice leading.

fundamentals.label: Definition
fundamentals.value: Four-note chord combining a diminished triad with a minor 7th

fundamentals.label: Sound Quality
fundamentals.value: Dark, yearning, unresolved - between minor 7th and fully diminished

fundamentals.label: Function
fundamentals.value: ii chord in minor keys (iiø7-V7-i), viiø7 in major keys

applications.label: Classical
applications.value: Supertonic in minor, leading-tone chord in major

boxes.title: Bm7b5 Example
items: Root: B (1st degree)
Minor 3rd: D (b3rd degree)
Diminished 5th: F (b5th degree)
Minor 7th: A (b7th degree)
Result: The ii chord in A minor (Bm7b5-E7-Am)

boxes.title: Interval Quality
items: Minor 3rd: Provides the dark, minor character
Diminished 5th (tritone): Creates tension needing resolution
Minor 7th: Softer than diminished 7th - the 'half' in half-diminished
Contains one tritone (root to b5), unlike dim7 which has two
Psychology: Yearning, bittersweet, seeking resolution

boxes.title: Scale Relationship
items: Built from: 7th degree of major scale (viiø7 in C major = Bm7b5)
Built from: 2nd degree of natural minor (iiø7 in A minor = Bm7b5)
Parent mode: Locrian (1-b2-b3-4-b5-b6-b7)
Jazz usage: Always think of it as iiø7 resolving to V7 to i
Function: Pre-dominant chord that sets up the V7 cadence

voicingGroups.tipDescription: These fundamental voicings cover the most common half-diminished shapes on guitar. The Bm7b5 is the most frequently encountered in jazz standards.

voicings.name: Dm7b5

voicings.name: Em7b5

voicingGroups.tipDescription: These voicings offer richer textures and smoother voice leading options for jazz and contemporary styles.

items.title: Minor ii-V-i (The Core Progression)

strumming.description: Jazz comping rhythm with swing feel

items.description: The most important minor-key jazz progression. The half-diminished chord creates a yearning pull toward the dominant, which resolves to minor tonic.

items.title: Extended Minor ii-V-i-iv
items.description: An extended minor-key progression commonly found in jazz ballads and Latin jazz. The half-diminished sets up a darker emotional arc.

items.title: viiø7 as Leading Tone Chord
items.description: The half-diminished chord built on the 7th degree of C major acts as a leading-tone chord, gently pulling back to the tonic.

items.title: Chromatic Half-Diminished Movement

strumming.pattern: D U D U D U D U

items.description: A classic minor-key turnaround. Starting on the tonic, the iiø7 introduces tension that resolves through V7 back home.

techniqueItems: Practice smooth voice leading from iiø7 to V7 - many notes are shared or move by half step
Learn the Bm7b5 shape thoroughly before moving to other roots
Compare the sound of m7b5 to regular m7 to internalize the b5 difference
Use a metronome and practice the ii-V-i cadence in all 12 minor keys
applicationItems: The iiø7-V7-i is the single most important minor-key progression in jazz
Half-diminished chords add sophistication to otherwise simple minor progressions
Voice leading from iiø7 to V7 is smoother than from iim7 to V7 in minor
Use half-diminished as a substitute for plain minor chords for richer harmony

practiceExercises.title: Practice Exercises
practiceExercises.tipDescription: These exercises focus on the most practical applications of half-diminished chords, emphasizing the minor ii-V-i cadence.

exercises.title: Exercise 1: Minor ii-V-i in All Keys
exercises.detail: Play the minor ii-V-i cadence through the cycle of fourths, using one voicing shape moved chromatically
exercises.tip: Focus on minimal finger movement - the b5 in the iiø7 resolves down by half step to the 3rd of the V7 chord

exercises.title: Exercise 2: Half-Diminished vs. Minor 7th Comparison
exercises.detail: Alternate between the minor 7th and half-diminished versions of each chord to train your ear to hear the b5 difference
exercises.tip: The only difference is one note (the 5th is lowered by one fret). Listen for the added darkness and tension.

exercises.title: Exercise 3: Voice Leading Through Minor Turnarounds
exercises.content: Turnaround: Am7 - Bm7b5 - E7 - Am7 (repeat in Dm, Gm, Cm)
exercises.detail: Practice the full minor turnaround focusing on smooth voice leading between each chord change
exercises.tip: Try to keep common tones ringing and move other voices by the smallest interval possible

concepts.title: Half-Diminished vs. Fully Diminished
items: Half-diminished (m7b5): 1-b3-b5-b7. Contains a minor 7th interval from root.
Fully diminished (dim7): 1-b3-b5-bb7. Contains a diminished 7th (enharmonic major 6th).
Half-diminished has ONE tritone (root to b5); fully diminished has TWO tritones.
The minor 7th in half-diminished gives it a softer, less symmetrical sound.
Locrian mode is the parent scale for half-diminished; Locrian b2 or diminished scale for dim7.

concepts.title: Reharmonization and Substitution Techniques
items: Any m7b5 chord shares 3 notes with the dominant 7th a minor 3rd below (e.g., Bm7b5 ~ G9).
Substitute iiø7 for iv6 in minor: Bm7b5 contains the same notes as Dm6 (D-F-A-B).
Locrian natural 2 (melodic minor 6th mode) provides a brighter scale choice over m7b5.
In modal jazz, treat half-diminished as a color chord rather than a functional pre-dominant.
Add the 9th (m9b5) or 11th (m11b5) for richer extensions in contemporary jazz.
